_doc: TRIGGER ANCHORS (operator 2026-08-01) — the dual-anchor half of rule retrieval. A rule is PLACED where its content compresses, but it must be RETRIEVED where the situations it governs land. Each entry seeds its rule text at each listed coord with src='trigger'. This file is the SOURCE; lens_rules is derived (seedRules DELETEs + rebuilds every reseed, so anchors live here and are re-applied by the seeder — never hand-INSERT into SQLite). curated = from the 2026-08-01 grading-pass miss families; learned = proposed by rule-trigger-anchors.mjs --learn from the trajectory spine. Keep rule text ≤240 chars (the seeder's cap).

anchors.rule: Measure, don't assert — when asked 'what measures did we add / could we compute', cite the computed series that exist (data/pmu/measure-history.ndjson · public/data/drift-series.json · rule-effectiveness.json), never a fresh exploration

anchors.rule: Never hand the operator a fork — no multiple-choice, no A/B/C menu; compute the answer, take the highest-confidence path, NAME the paths not taken and bifurcate them to rooms; read the transcript momentum before asking anything
anchors.why: open-ended verdict prompts ('is this good enough?') are the worst offPct family (71-97%) and land at the C,C degenerate magnet; the NEVER-FORK line was never seeded (240ch cap dropped it)
